reason: The hypothesis transfers the melamine-driven solvation strategy, previously studied only in room-temperature electrocatalytic oxygen reduction, to the harsh high-temperature oxidative environment of automotive exhaust catalysis, a regime where organic modifiers are generally considered unstable. It combines this with the concept of atomic-scale electronic modification from Pt-trimer decoration, proposing a new application that no passage suggests.

melamine disrupts hydrogen bonding and alters solvation to weaken OH adsorption (P9)
charge localization induced by atomic-scale decoration improves performance (P1, P4, P8)
